AN05B023a-d: dimorphic partners, by volume

What this asks

The pair pages each answer “which of these two sends more of its output to dimorphic or sex-specific partners” for one pair. This asks it of the whole AN05B023 family at once, so the members are ranked against each other rather than two at a time.

Each member is fetched separately and normalised by its own total output, so frac is a share and members of different sizes stay comparable.

options(rgl.useNULL = TRUE)   # must precede any library that pulls rgl in (nat)

suppressMessages({
  library(neuprintr); library(malecns); library(nat)
  library(coconatfly); library(coconat)
  options(malecns.dataset = "male-cns:v1.0")   # malecns helpers ignore MCNS_DATASET
  library(dplyr); library(tibble)
  library(ggplot2); library(ggrepel); library(scales); library(patchwork)
})

R_DIR <- "/Users/fkampf/Documents/pheromone.paper/analyses/an_investigation/R"

Sys.setenv(AN_CASE = "an05b023bc")   # only for FOCUS and the palettes
source(file.path(R_DIR, "_paths.R"))
source(file.path(R_DIR, "_an_pair.R"))
neuprint_login(server = MCNS_SERVER, dataset = MCNS_DATASET)
load_once <- function(name, expr, envir = .GlobalEnv) {
  # eval() here evaluates a quote()d expression written literally in this file -
  # a lazy-evaluation idiom for "only fetch if not already cached", not a parser
  # of external input.
  if (!exists(name, envir = envir, inherits = FALSE)) {
    assign(name, eval(expr), envir = envir)
  }
  get(name, envir = envir)
}

mba <- load_once("mba", quote(mcns_body_annotations()))

contact_pool <- sensory_pool(mba)

MEMBERS <- sort(unique(grep("^AN05B023[a-z]$", mba$type, value = TRUE)))
MEMBERS
## [1] "AN05B023a" "AN05B023b" "AN05B023c" "AN05B023d"

Whole reconstruction

fam <- dimorph_output_family(MEMBERS, mba, contact_pool)

fam |>
  filter(dimorphism != "not annotated") |>
  summarise(annotated_share = sum(frac), synapses = sum(synapses),
            partner_types = sum(partner_types), .by = member)
dimorph_family_plot(fam, MEMBERS)

VNC only

The whole-reconstruction numbers are not comparable across this family, because AN05B023b is cut off in the brain — see 08_an05b023bc_cut.Rmd. Anything a member does in the brain is missing from b by construction, so the same query restricted to the VNC is the one place all four are scored on a volume they all have.

fam_vnc <- dimorph_output_family(MEMBERS, mba, contact_pool, roi = "VNC")

fam_vnc |>
  filter(dimorphism != "not annotated") |>
  summarise(annotated_share = sum(frac), synapses = sum(synapses),
            partner_types = sum(partner_types), .by = member)
dimorph_family_plot(fam_vnc, MEMBERS,
                    "share of that type's VNC downstream output")

Brain only

The VNC panel says AN05B023c barely works with dimorphic partners in the nerve cord. The whole-reconstruction panel says it does about as much of it as the others. Both can be true if it does that work in the brain, and this panel is where that claim is testable. CentralBrain is the ROI, so the optic lobes are out.

fam_brain <- dimorph_output_family(MEMBERS, mba, contact_pool,
                                   roi = "CentralBrain")

fam_brain |>
  filter(dimorphism != "not annotated") |>
  summarise(annotated_share = sum(frac), synapses = sum(synapses),
            partner_types = sum(partner_types), .by = member)
dimorph_family_plot(fam_brain, MEMBERS,
                    "share of that type's brain downstream output")

It is testable and it holds. On the run of 2026-08-13 AN05B023c gives 20.8% of its brain output to annotated dimorphic partners, over 1291 synapses and 64 partner types, against 3.7% in the VNC. AN05B023d is beside it at 21.8%, over 1966 synapses and 83 types. AN05B023a is at 6.9% and AN05B023b at 10.0%, and AN05B023b’s bar rests on 43 synapses out of a brain output of 431, which is the truncation again rather than a result.

So the whole-reconstruction ranking is a mixture of two different behaviours, and splitting it by volume separates them: in the brain c and d are the dimorphic ones, in the VNC they are not.

Brain input

The three panels above ask what a member sends. This asks what it receives, and it asks it in the brain, because that is where AN05B023c does the dimorphic work the VNC panel says it does not do in the nerve cord.

CentralBrain is the ROI, so the optic lobes are out. Sensory partners are dropped, as they are on the output side, so this counts central input only.

Read the denominators before the bars. On the run of 2026-08-13 the whole brain input was AN05B023a 4745 synapses, AN05B023d 880, AN05B023c 331 and AN05B023b 56. AN05B023b has no bar at all: 56 synapses, none of them from an annotated dimorphic type. So this panel compares one well-sampled member against two thinly-sampled ones, and AN05B023c’s share rests on 89 synapses.

fam_brain_in <- dimorph_input_family(MEMBERS, mba, contact_pool,
                                     roi = "CentralBrain")

fam_brain_in |>
  filter(dimorphism != "not annotated") |>
  summarise(annotated_share = sum(frac), synapses = sum(synapses),
            partner_types = sum(partner_types), .by = member)
dimorph_family_plot(fam_brain_in, MEMBERS,
                    "share of that type's brain input")

Taken with the VNC panel, AN05B023c reads the same way on both sides of the synapse: what it does with dimorphic partners, it does in the brain. The sampling is too thin to put a number on that, and the sensible next step is the per-partner list rather than a larger share.

The two views disagree

They disagree enough that quoting only the first would be wrong. On the run of 2026-08-12 the whole-reconstruction shares were a 11.7%, b 10.3%, c 13.9%, d 15.6% — d highest, and the four within a few points of each other. Restricted to the VNC they were a 12.8%, b 10.1%, c 3.7%, d 9.6%: the ranking inverts and AN05B023c drops by nearly four fold.

That is a statement about AN05B023c. Its output onto dimorphic partners is almost entirely a brain phenomenon, and it barely does this in the VNC at all — which is also why the b-versus-c comparison in 05_an05b023bc.Rmd cannot settle the question on its own, since b has no brain arbor to compare with.

AN05B023a and AN05B023b hold their share in both views, so for them the number is about the neuron rather than about which volume was counted.

Two caveats that apply to every bar here. not annotated is the majority class in mba, so all bars are short by construction and the comparison is between them, not against 100%. And the VNC panel does not repair AN05B023b: if that reconstruction is also incomplete inside the VNC, its share is computed over an output that is itself missing synapses.

Where these families sit among ascending neurons

The pages in this project look at three families. This puts them in the field. Every ascending type that takes even one synapse from the leg and wing gustatory bristles is included, and the bars are that type’s whole output, summed over its bodies.

Two things to keep in mind while reading it. A type with fourteen bodies outranks a type with two on cell count alone, which is why n_bodies is in the table. And nothing here is thresholded on the sensory side: the median type takes about 40 synapses from the pool, so the right-hand half of the ranking is made of neurons that barely touch contact chemosensation at all.

asc_rank <- ascending_contact_ranking(mba, contact_pool)

asc_rank |>
  mutate(rank = row_number()) |>
  filter(grepl("^AN05B023|^AN05B102|^AN09B017", type)) |>
  select(rank, type, total_out, n_bodies, sensory_syn)
ascending_rank_plot(asc_rank)

None of the three families is near the top. The largest ascending outputs in this set belong to types this project does not work on, and the marked families sit in the middle of the distribution. That is the right context for every share on this page: these are ordinary-sized ascending neurons, picked for what they connect to rather than for how much they output.
